applies_why: The text weighs a chain-against-chain collision, the challenger's seed/loins chain versus the defender's chain at D6 vs C1, which is exactly the collision K-C governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: Phrase: 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.' Reading one: the retirement bars only dismissing pressed witnesses because no verse states the contrary, leaving a judge free to hedge a footed chain for lacking an explicit statement of its own conclusion. Reading two: the retirement bars any statement-absence discount at the seat, on either side's chain, so footing is the only permitted weight. I chose reading two, because the judge first granted the challenger's chain footing and then discounted it solely for not naming its conclusion, a statement-absence consideration, while the defender's parallel hedge ('rests on the woman-route inference') is a footing consideration.
why: Having granted the challenger's chain footing, the judge still discounts it because no verse names Joseph as the begetter, weighing the collision partly by the explicit-statement test that K-C retires at a judge's seat for either side rather than by footing alone.
